result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [DataScan.save_to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Save the profile to a JSON file. twitter-card: title: >- [DataScan.save_to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Save the profile to a JSON file. title: >- [DataScan.save_to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Save the profile to a JSON file. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Save the profile to a JSON file. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/datascan.py#L839-L890){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature DataScan.save_to_json(output_file) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Saving a scan to a file is the simplest way to keep a baseline: scan a table once, save the profile, and load it later with [`load_from_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.load_from_json`) to compare a new scan against it with [`compare()`](`pointblank.DataScan.compare`). The file holds the output of [`to_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.to_json`), so it's small (it stores the statistics, not the data) and can be kept in version control next to the code that produces the table. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [output_file]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path to the output JSON file. An existing file is overwritten. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nothing is returned. The profile is written to `output_file`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's save a profile of the `small_table` dataset to a file in a temporary directory. ::: {#d051ae9f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import tempfile from pathlib import Path small_table = pb.load_dataset(dataset="small_table", tbl_type="polars") profile_path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "small_table_profile.json" pb.DataScan(small_table, tbl_name="small_table").save_to_json(profile_path) print(profile_path.read_text()[:180]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { "metadata": { "table_name": "small_table", "row_count": 13, "columns": [ "date_time", "date", "a", "b" ``` ::: ::: The file starts with the table's metadata, and the column profiles follow. Loading it with [`load_from_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.load_from_json`) gives back the same profile, without needing the table itself.
